transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um, well, I came in today because I'm just having a really hard time focusing at work. I'm a high school teacher, and I can sit down with a stack of essays or a new curriculum document, fully intending to get it done. But within ten minutes, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same page. My mind will be on three completely different things, and I'm barely taking in a single word of what's right in front of me. It's getting really frustrating.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively worried or anxious about things, even when there isn't a clear reason for it?

No, not really. I mean, I definitely get stressed out when I'm falling behind on my grading or lesson plans, but I wouldn't say I feel anxious for no reason. It's mostly just frustration about the work itself, not a general worry about other things.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
No, I haven't. I mean, I still enjoy my hobbies and everything when I actually have free time. I don't feel depressed or anything like that. It's really just the focus issue that's bothering me.
Outside of work, do you find it hard to organize tasks or stay focused on things that need to be done, like household chores or even following through with plans?

Yeah, definitely. It's not just at school. At home, I'll start doing the dishes, and then I'll remember I need to take out the trash, so I'll go do that. But on the way, I'll see a piece of mail I meant to open, so I'll put the trash bag down to look at it... and then an hour later, the dishes are still in the sink, the trash is sitting in the hallway, and I haven't really finished anything. It's just hard to stick with one chore until it's done. And with plans, I don't mean to, but I'm late a lot because I lose track of time or get sidetracked right before I'm supposed to leave.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble focusing or staying on task even when you were a child, like in elementary school?

Yeah, actually. I remember my parents always finding, like, crumpled up worksheets at the bottom of my backpack that I just completely forgot to turn in. And my report cards back in elementary school almost always said the same kind of things. Teachers would write that I was "bright but careless," or that I wouldn't finish my work unless someone was standing right there supervising me. So, yeah, it's definitely been a thing since I was a kid.
As a child or even now, do you often feel restless, have trouble staying seated, or act on impulse without thinking things through?

No, not really. I don't really have an issue with sitting still or feeling restless. It's more about my mind wandering than my body needing to move. And I wouldn't say I'm impulsive, either. I usually think things through, I just... have trouble actually getting them done. So, no, the physical restlessness and acting without thinking haven't really been a problem for me.
